title: An old mansion
goal: Use the passive, the reflexive and kendi together, and follow the story of an old house that became a museum.

intro.text: History is told in the passive: *Konak 1880'de yapıldı, 2015'te onarıldı ve müze olarak açıldı* (The mansion was built in 1880, restored in 2015 and opened as a museum). This lesson brings the whole unit together.

vocab.en: to seem, to look; to appear

exercises.title: Bir konağın hikâyesi
exercises.passage:
Eski şehrin ortasında, büyük bir bahçenin içinde iki katlı, beyaz bir konak var. Konak 1880'de bir tüccar ailesi için yapıldı. Duvarları taştan, odaları geniş ve aydınlık. Aile bu evde neredeyse yüz yıl yaşadı.

1970'lerde aile İstanbul'a taşındı ve konak boş kaldı. Yıllarca kimse ona bakmadı. Pencereler kırıldı, çatı bir kış yağmurunda çöktü. Bir ara bazı insanlar konağı yıkıp yerine bir apartman yapmak istediler.

Sonunda belediye konağı satın aldı. Konak üç yılda onarıldı ve 2015'te müze olarak açıldı. Bugün odalarda ailenin eşyaları sergileniyor: eski mobilyalar, fotoğraflar, mektuplar. Yukarıdaki salonda her ay yeni bir sergi açılıyor.

Müze pazartesi günleri kapalı, diğer günler giriş ücretsiz. Müzenin içinde fotoğraf çekilmez. Ziyaretçiler konağı kendi başlarına gezebilir ya da bir rehberle gezebilir. Konak bugün yeni gibi görünüyor, ama her taşının bir hikâyesi var.

glossary.en: middle (şehrin ortasında: in the middle of the town)

exercises.translation: In the middle of the old town, inside a large garden, there is a white two-storey mansion. It was built in 1880 for a merchant family. Its walls are of stone, its rooms large and full of light. The family lived in this house for almost a hundred years. In the 1970s the family moved to Istanbul and the mansion stood empty. For years nobody looked after it. The windows were broken, and the roof caved in one winter in the rain. At one point some people wanted to pull it down and put up an apartment building in its place. In the end the town council bought the mansion. It was restored in three years and opened as a museum in 2015. Today the family's belongings are on display in the rooms: old furniture, photographs, letters. In the hall upstairs a new exhibition opens every month. The museum is closed on Mondays; on other days entry is free. No photographs are allowed inside the museum. Visitors can walk around the mansion on their own or with a guide. Today the mansion looks as good as new, but every one of its stones has a story.

questions.q: Who was the mansion built for?
questions.explain: *Konak 1880'de bir tüccar ailesi için yapıldı*: the passive, **was built for**.

questions.q: What happened to the house after the family left?
options: It stood empty and fell into ruin
questions.explain: *Konak boş kaldı … Pencereler kırıldı, çatı … çöktü.*

questions.q: Which sentence states a rule for visitors?
questions.explain: The negative aorist of the passive states a rule: *çek-il-mez*, **no photographs**.

questions.q: What does *kendi başlarına* tell you about the visitors?
options: They can walk around on their own
They must stay with a guide
They have to come in groups
questions.explain: *Kendi başına* is **on one's own**; with *-ları*, **on their own**.

exercises.text: Konak 2015'te onar___ ve müze olarak açıldı.
exercises.en: The mansion was restored in 2015 and opened as a museum.

reject.why: *Onardı* is active, **he restored**. The mansion **was restored**: *onar-ıl-dı*.
`-In` is only for stems in l; *onar-* ends in r: *onarıldı*.

exercises.prompt: The walls were repaired last year.

reject.why: *Onardı* is active: the walls would be the ones repairing. **Were repaired**: *onar-ıl-dı*.

exercises.question: *Bu kubbe 16. yüzyılda yapılmış.* How does the speaker know?
options: She read it or was told

why.1: Nobody alive saw it built; and for something you witnessed, *yapıldı* would be the form.
why.2: `-mIş` is about what you've learned, not what you will learn.

exercises.explain: `-mIş` after the passive: *yap-ıl-mış*, history the speaker has learned rather than seen.

accept: The exhibition will open tomorrow at ten.
The exhibition will open at ten (o'clock) tomorrow.
The exhibition will open tomorrow at ten o'clock.
The exhibition will be opened tomorrow at ten (o'clock).
The exhibition will be opened at ten (o'clock) tomorrow.
The exhibition opens tomorrow at ten (o'clock).

exercises.label: *kendi* + possessive + accusative, as an object: myself, yourself…
exercises.explain: *kendi* takes the possessive of the person, then the case: *kendi-m-i*, *kendi-n-i*. For **himself** or **herself**, *kendini* or *kendisini*.

exercises.en: How do you get to the mansion? By bus?
exercises.explain: *gid-il-ir*: the impersonal passive asks how **anyone** gets there. *Gider* would be **how does he go**.

exercises.prompt: Did you make this cake yourself?
accept: Bu pastayı kendi başına mı yaptın?
Bu pastayı kendi başınıza mı yaptınız?
Sen bu pastayı kendin mi yaptın?

reject.why: *Kendini* would make **yourself** the object, the thing made. As **in person**, *kendin* stays in the nominative: *kendin mi yaptın?*

exercises.question: *Sabah yıkandım, giyindim ve hazırlandım.* What did the speaker do?
options: Had a wash, got dressed and got ready
Washed the clothes and prepared breakfast
Was washed and dressed by someone else

why.1: Washing clothes would be *çamaşırları yıkadım*, with the plain verb and an object.
why.2: With the speaker doing the actions, these read as reflexive: she did them to herself.

exercises.explain: Three reflexive verbs: *yıka-n-*, *giy-in-*, *hazırla-n-*, all done to oneself.

accept: The dome of the mosque is made of stone.
The mosque's dome is made of stone.
The [dome of the mosque|mosque's dome] [was made|was built|has been built] (out) of stone.
The [dome of the mosque|mosque's dome] is built (out) of stone.
The [dome of the mosque|mosque's dome] is made out of stone.
